brief: c299: the martins' second mud source is the same in every world. #202 gave the colony a strand — `martStrandF()` off the river's drying bank — but the strand is built from `hash()`, which is NOT seeded, so a rainless colony now founds on the SAME days in every seed and the worlds differ only in which birds turn up. LAWS.md states the rule this breaks: hash() is one town in every world, and a per-day hash is one sample of the calendar in every seed — SALT it when the calendar must differ per world. Put a per-world salt on the level's lag so the mud year runs on a per-town clock, the way the cart's calendar (WIND_SALT) and the fair's (isFairDay) already do. Price it as the laws require: histogram the founding day over the YEAR across six seeds on HEAD and on the candidate, and show the distribution is the same SHAPE with the seeds no longer in lockstep — this is a fidelity fix, not a behaviour change, and the colony's size and timing must not move.
successLooksLike: Founding day across six seeds spreads instead of coinciding, while the per-seed distribution over a year keeps HEAD's shape and the colony's mean size is inside the seed noise. Name the salt in the source next to the two that precede it.
avoid: Do not spend an R() draw on this — the strand is hashed and must stay hashed, or every downstream draw in the world reshuffles (LAWS.md: any new draw reshuffles the whole seeded world). Do not touch MART_WET or the rain source; only the strand's clock is at issue.
